title: TokenGuard: AI cost per customer and spending caps for small SaaS companies
source: Top 25 SaaS ideas for Victor (research report, Nov 2026)
summary: Shows small SaaS companies which customers and features lose them money on AI API costs, and stops runaway usage with per-customer spending caps.
hook: "One customer used our AI feature so much that he cost us more than he paid, and we only found out from the bill."
story:
**Priya is CTO of a 6-person SaaS startup** that added an AI writing feature. The OpenAI bill grows every month, but she cannot see **which customers or plans** cause it. Last month one free-trial user ran thousands of requests overnight.

She tried an open-source logging tool, but it shows tokens and traces, not business answers like **"which plan loses money on AI?"**. She wants per-customer costs next to Stripe revenue, and hard caps that switch heavy users to a cheaper model instead of failing.
whyNow: Several small-team AI usage tools were bought by bigger firms in 2026, according to secondary sources: Langfuse by ClickHouse (January), Helicone put into maintenance mode after Mintlify bought it (March), and Portkey by Palo Alto Networks (May). That may leave small users looking for a simple alternative.
evidence: More than 80% of companies say AI costs eroded gross margin by more than 6% [CIO.com]
Firms are using up annual AI budgets within months [McKinsey]
A Harness survey of 700 leaders says about 26% of AI spend is wasted [IT Brew]
2026 acquisitions of Langfuse, Helicone and Portkey reported by secondary blogs [DevelopersDigest / FutureAGI]
These surveys mostly describe larger companies [Top 25 report]
